hints: Convert the 300 lines/mm into the slit spacing $d$ in metres using $d = 1/300$ mm for the 450 nm light.
Use the grating equation $d \sin\theta = n\lambda$ for normal incidence and set $\sin\theta = 1$ to find the largest possible order $n$.
Remember total maxima means counting $+n$ and $-n$ orders on both sides plus the $n = 0$ central maximum, not just the value of $n$.
walkthrough: Find the grating spacing from $N = 300$ lines per mm: $d = \frac{1.0 \times 10^{-3}}{300} = 3.33 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$.
State the condition for an intensity maximum at normal incidence: $d \sin\theta = n\lambda$, with $\lambda = 450 \text{ nm} = 450 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$.
The largest order occurs at the largest $\sin\theta = 1$, so $n_{max} = \frac{d}{\lambda} = \frac{3.33 \times 10^{-6}}{450 \times 10^{-9}} \approx 7.4$.
Only whole orders exist, so $n_{max} = 7$. Orders $n = 1$ to $7$ appear on each side of the central beam.
Add both sides plus the zero order: total $= 2 \times 7 + 1 = 15$. This is option D.

options.A: This is the highest order $n = 7$ on one side only, not the total count on both sides plus the zero order.
options.B: This counts orders on one side plus zero but omits the matching orders on the opposite side of the beam.
options.C: This is $2 \times 7$ and counts both sides but omits the $n = 0$ central maximum.
options.D: Maximum order is $n = 7$, so $7$ orders each side plus $n = 0$ gives $15$ maxima in total.
